title: Choose the look for TenderAssist
question: One direction is assigned; you can keep it, take an alternative, re-roll, or go with the plain category standard.

options.label: Ink & Stamp
options.lineage: Indian office rubber stamps in violet ink on plain office paper
options.thesis: Every decision is stamped: a tender you approve or reject gets a dated ink mark, the way an office file does.
options.viewport: A violet side rail (Today, Tenders, Runs, Settings); Today opens with Find tenders (from/to dates, Start) and below it one tender at a time to decide, Approve / Reject / Later.
options.risk: Stamps turn into a gimmick if used for anything but decisions and finished dates.

raised.raise: Violet ink owns the whole side rail at full strength, not a scattered accent.
Reject and Stop sit apart from Approve and Start, with deliberate space between them.
One reserved ink marks 'you are here': the active date and the step needing you.
Every tender card keeps value, closing date and department in the same fixed places.
The date strip holds every date at one size on one line, so 21 dates read as a sequence.

options.label: Office Tender File
options.lineage: the green and buff government file cover with tags and a noting sheet
options.thesis: Each tender is a file: a cover with its facts, tabs for details and documents, and a noting sheet where the decision is written.
options.viewport: Green file-cover header on each tender, tabs for Details / Documents / Decision; Today lists files waiting like a tray.
options.risk: The most familiar office metaphor, and buff paper drifts toward the cream look every tool ships.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport boarding pass and live departures board
options.thesis: A date range runs like a departures board: each date a row, the current one lit, finished ones dropping off; each tender a segmented pass.
options.viewport: A board of dates (status, tenders found, kept) beside the portal; deciding shows each tender as a pass with fixed segments.
options.case: Fuses strongly for multi-date runs and progress; less natural for calmly deciding tenders.
options.risk: Can feel like a monitoring screen rather than an office tool.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: black and white barcode data art
options.thesis: Tenders as a dense black-and-white data field.
options.viewport: Columns of tender numbers in pure black and white.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cold and strobing for a calm daily office tool.
options.kept: Total palette commitment: violet owns the rail.

options.label: Dark Console
options.thesis: A graphite working surface split by hairline seams.
options.viewport: Persistent dark panels around the portal.
options.case: Fuses poorly: reads as a programmer's tool, not an office's.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated from their neighbours.
options.risk: Technical feel you asked to avoid.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A run as a course of numbered controls in purple.
options.viewport: Dates as numbered controls on a course line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a sport's map language the operator does not read.
options.kept: One reserved ink for 'you are here'.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Tenders as a ranked roster of cards.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of tender cards.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful, which you ruled out.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A date range as a sequence of same-scale plates.
options.viewport: Dates as aligned plates on one baseline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: cream and engraving, an editorial costume.
options.kept: Same size and baseline across a sequence.
options.risk: The cream look every tool ships.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, light business app: white panels, grey text, one blue accent, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Side menu, a header, and tidy lists and forms you already know.
canonCard.risk: Clear but forgettable; looks like every other admin tool.
